context: Current closing price of RTX Corp (RTX): $189.53 USD as of 2026-11-06.
justification_text:
The point estimates at each time horizon represent my best guess of the likely outcome for the variable of interest, based on the available data and trends at the time of the forecast. In this case, you’ll notice that the point estimate remains the same across all time horizons—189.53. This implies that, on average, I expected the value to hold steady over one day, one week, and one month. This could suggest either that the underlying variable was relatively stable historically or that there were no clear signals pointing to an upward or downward trend in the near future. Essentially, the model inferred that the best prediction at all horizons was continuity.

The widening confidence intervals reflect growing uncertainty as time horizons lengthen. In the short term (one day), the forecast is highly influenced by immediate dynamics, such as recent price movement, volatility, or daily noise, leading to a narrow range of outcomes. However, as you extend to one week, and particularly one month, more factors come into play—larger shifts in market conditions, potential new data releases, or more distant external events—creating a broader range of plausible outcomes. This is why the 90% confidence interval is tightest at one day (187.37 to 191.69) and widest at one month (178.38 to 200.68).

Certain risks or events could push outcomes outside these intervals, even though they are designed to capture 90% of the likely results. For example, unexpected shocks like geopolitical events, major policy changes, or unexpected announcements (earnings surprises, regulatory updates, etc.) could cause outcomes to deviate significantly. Other sources of risk might include systemic financial instability or unpredictable investor behavior that amplifies volatility. If such events occur, the simple assumption of stability underlying the point estimate and the rate of uncertainty growth may no longer hold, making the intervals insufficient to capture reality.
